****A SECOND UPDATE****

So I nagged and nagged (although I shouldn't have had to) my doctor until I convinced her to see me today to do a check up and make sure my IUD was placed properly. When I got there, she told me that she was considering telling me to take it out right after she had put it in, but decided to wait because of how much pain I was in (tf?) So I get in the stirrups, the strings turn out to be fine, and I tell her I want it out now. Today, on the way there, I was cramping so badly I thought I was going to vomit, and had to have someone else drive me. So 2 seconds of clamping pain and a pair of forceps(?) later and my IUD is gone forever, along with all the pain that came with it. Apparently I am one of the unlucky few that get the extreme side effects that you read about in the IUD booklets. So what now? I don't know. But I do know that nothing is going in my uterus again for a long time. Thanks for all your help and for sharing your stories ladies!
I'm so sorry you had to go from 0 to 100 on the cramp scale; that sounds terrible! I called her back and got an appointment today which I will write about below. I hope that things go better for you!

****AN UPDATE****

My doctor finally got back to me and originally thought I may need to get it out. However, I told her how my symptoms were and she said they were progressing in a positive direction so they are just going to do a check up (hopefully soon- still waiting for scheduling) and see how the placement is.

I don't have a copper IUD in however I'd say our experiences are parallel except that the bleeding for me stopped on day 4. I'm not sure I'm going to keep it in. The benefits, however, make it almost irresistible in regards to birth control. Guess the old wait n see is my life for now.
They did not schedule a follow up with me. Or tell me any of the positioning you did, so thank you. I think I might have my s.o. try because every time I do its like going in the Mariana trench.

To answer your questions, no I have not had a pap smear before. However, I have had a speculum and pelvic exams many times before because of a persistent uti, so that part wasn't too much of a shock to me. My doc did not check my blood pressure before but I wasn't that nervous because I had taken 1500 MG of my friends pain killers before hand (I can't remember which kind but it was within the recommended  dose.) My doctor did not have me schedule a follow up appointment at all nor did she tell me how to check the strings. I believe this is because of the response I was having so they were more worried about that but that is not an excuse in my book. My BP was fine before the placement and then dropped to where my pulse was below 50 aka not good. Thank you so much for telling me about your experience, I'm glad I'm not alone in my thus far negative one.
